source_uncertainties: Manifest labels26/27 retained. Publisher opening cues read Week09 Lecture31 and Week10 Lecture32. This is a numbering offset of5 labels, not a timestamp shift; no seconds subtracted or inferred.

vN1CmWmaNOU duration3464s in manifest versus3463s transcript.json; metadata uses actual transcript media_duration3463. X7hh5E4q2kE duration3035s agrees. Caption endpoints3458.32/3026.6s cover closing summaries; videos intentionally deleted before run; no playback/recovery claimed.

L26 captions3334-3367 omit the minus in Vy; full frames f0112/f0114 show Vy=-psi_x. L27 f0020/f0024 confirm. L27 captions631-653 also garble the substituted signs; board f0024 gives -psi_xx-psi_yy=0, so chapter derives omega=-Laplacian psi.

L26 circulation/irrotational equivalence stated without global topology qualification (2250-2310s, board f0083). Chapter restricts Stokes to a regular spanning surface; one zero loop is insufficient; every-loop global criterion differs from local curl. Annular counterexample is original.

Kelvin board f0083 omits separate density/smoothness conditions. Chapter proves constant-density smooth conservative-force case, identifies material loop, and qualifies barotropic extension. Original Thomson1869 paper not consulted; no page or historical-priority claim.

L26 circular free-vortex element arrows are schematic (f0039/f0040). Zero local spin does not keep every material line orientation fixed when strain is nonzero; chapter uses mean-edge definition and explicitly qualifies this.

L27 f0088 writes unsteady spatial constant without explicit t dependence. Chapter B(t) has zero spatial gradient, may vary in time; gauge derivative tracked. Steady Bernoulli global scalar is proved directly from Euler, without assuming a global single-valued velocity potential.

General scalar stream function is planar incompressible, not every conceivable flow. Local/global existence and3D vector-potential/symmetry boundaries are stated. L27 captions overstate unrestricted generality.

No source equations or symbols remain dependent on unreadable frames. Early f0006 occlusion resolved by f0010; f0090 is an erased transitional frame, while f0088 supplies unsteady relation and f0101 steady summary.

Only consulted external primary research is Iftimie etal2013v1; original papers it cites were not opened. Its higher-regularity exterior-domain velocity reconstruction is not claimed for arbitrary domains; weak-solution findings are not imported.
Illustrative rho1000kg/m3, strain rates, lengths, pressures and source strengths are chosen model inputs, not empirical property values.

Figures were rendered/viewed privately through PyMuPDF SVG conversion. That preview suppresses SVG dash arrays; dashed/dotted attributes are present in final SVG source. Actual shared-reader/browser appearance remains lead validation, not an author acceptance claim.

sections.section: A fluid domain, a velocity field, and boundary data
sections.teaching_construction: Formal model: regular fluid domain, fields, density, boundary data. Original 2m by1m turning flow V=(ax,-ay), a=.5/s.

sections.section: What removing viscosity does to the equations
sections.lecture_material: Outer inviscid region, mu=0 Euler equations; first-order velocity derivatives, nonlinearity and inability to superpose general Euler solutions.
sections.teaching_construction: Constitutive versus kinematic distinction; complete local Euler/continuity definitions and Reynolds-force scaling boundary.

sections.section: Local rotation is different from streamline curvature
sections.lecture_material: Symmetric/skew velocity gradient, omega=2Omega, planar curl; free/forced vortex; straight Couette streamlines; viscous wall layer versus outer flow; uniform viscous irrotational counterexample, inviscid rotational possibilities.
sections.teaching_construction: Explicit mean-edge rotation argument, polar curl calculation, units and numerical tests, material-line versus local-spin qualification, running pure strain.

sections.section: Circulation and the surface required by Stokes' theorem
sections.lecture_material: Circulation definition, Stokes surface interpretation, planar vorticity integral, irrotationality discussion.
sections.research_extension: Iftimie2013 pp3-4,8: separate boundary circulations and vorticity in exterior domains.
sections.teaching_construction: Orientation, units, valid spanning surface, small-loop versus one-loop distinction, annular counterexample and2pi normalization.

sections.section: Why initially irrotational fluid can stay irrotational
sections.lecture_material: Kelvin circulation theorem for inviscid flow with conservative force; initially irrotational flow stays irrotational.
sections.research_extension: Iftimie2013 p3 explicitly distinguishes classical smooth Kelvin circulation conservation.
sections.teaching_construction: Smooth constant-density material-loop proof including moving line element; barotropic qualification, moving rectangular-loop check, singularity boundary.

sections.section: Constructing a velocity potential, locally and globally
sections.lecture_material: Closed-loop split through two paths, endpoint difference, V=grad phi; potential-flow terminology.
sections.teaching_construction: Local/global topology conditions; precise every-loop criterion, gauge, rectangle path check, annular branch potential and Figure13.1.

sections.section: A two-dimensional stream function and the flux it measures
sections.lecture_material: Streamline tangency, stream surfaces/tubes, planar slope, psi levels and flow differences, Vx=psi_y,Vy=-psi_x;3D vector representation remark.
sections.teaching_construction: Compatibility proof from planar continuity, signed flux right-normal convention, rectangle1m2/s, polar transformation, global flux obstruction/source normalization, qualified3D scope.

sections.section: Continuity and irrotationality give two Laplace equations
sections.lecture_material: Potential definition review, incompressible continuity yields harmonic phi; stream function satisfies continuity identically, irrotationality yields harmonic psi; scalar2D versus3D comparison.
sections.teaching_construction: Both hinges explicit; rotational Poisson comparison with Couette, compressible mass equation boundary, rectangle derivative cancellation.

sections.lecture_material: Linear combination of harmonic solutions, simple building blocks, Euler nonlinearity contrast. Final3022s warning: pressure does not superpose.
sections.teaching_construction: Common regular domain, homogeneous/inhomogeneous boundary data, uniform addition fails left wall despite local equations, kinetic cross term.

sections.section: Impermeable walls, open boundaries, and uniqueness
sections.lecture_material: Fixed solid no penetration; psi constant on body, phi normal derivative zero; prescribed uniform far-field components.
sections.teaching_construction: Moving-wall generalization, no-slip distinction, rectangle complete Neumann data and compatibility; single-valued Neumann uniqueness proof and annular limit; far-field growth/gauge.

sections.section: Orthogonal level curves and a consistent complex convention
sections.lecture_material: Equipotential and streamline definitions, differential/slope argument for orthogonal intersections.
sections.teaching_construction: Coordinate-free gradient check, regular-point/stagnation qualification, numerical slopes, computed Figure13.2; optional complex coordinate/convention derived from definitions.

sections.section: Recovering pressure and the extent of Bernoulli's constant
sections.lecture_material: Planar Euler equations, conservative gravity-height force, irrotational substitution, x/y gradient equations, spatial Bernoulli constant; steady streamline/everywhere distinction; velocity superposition versus pressure warning.
sections.teaching_construction: Vector identity checked by components, unsteady B(t)/gauge, direct steady proof independent of global phi, rectangle cross-streamline375Pa and3component Euler check, annular pressure375Pa.

sections.section: Executable checks of local equations, flux, and a hole
sections.teaching_construction: Standard-library finite differences, regular annulus stencils, boundary residual, flux and circular quadrature, pressure arithmetic, actual sign/wall mutations and rejected inputs.
Model-specific conclusions, circulation information, wall-layer/compressible/rotational/singularity boundaries and ordered diagnostic checks.

Six full solutions: general linear field, annular two paths, incompatible boundary design, circulation-radius computational comparison, unsteady/gauge pressure, singular source at corner and global mass balance.
